title: The Rough Landfall
premise: Cyrus Nakamura, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover equipment from an expedition that went silent upriver in the Kestrel Basin. With a ragged crew—a disgraced hydrologist, a teenage radio prodigy, and a syndicate enforcer sent to watch him—Cyrus follows the river toward its forbidden source, where the missing expedition found something worth killing for: a mineral deposit that could rewrite weather prediction, and therefore power. As the monsoon closes in and the syndicate's true intentions surface, Cyrus must choose between paying his debt with betrayal or burning his old life down. In the end he destroys the survey data rather than let it be weaponized, loses the enforcer who became his closest ally, and returns downstream with nothing but his crew's trust—finally measuring life in people instead of miles.
about_author: Odile Ravensworth is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running freight through monsoon country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose survival depends on reading water, weather, and each other correctly.

chapters.title: Debt of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Cyrus Nakamura, POV. Chasing a supercell across the flats to earn storm data money, Cyrus calculates how many more seasons he needs to clear his debt to the Vane Syndicate. A syndicate collector intercepts him at a fuel stop with an offer: one salvage job upriver wipes the slate clean. Beat: restless desperation disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: The Silent Frequency
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The missing Meridian Expedition's last radio transmissions play on loop in a syndicate office—calm coordinates, then static. Cyrus recognizes the voice as Dr. Ilsa Reyes, a hydrologist he once worked with. He signs the contract knowing the job is wrong. Beat: dread settling under the lure of freedom.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. At the river town of Lowmark, Cyrus assembles his team: Priya Osei, a hydrologist drummed out of academia; Tuck, a sixteen-year-old radio prodigy with no last name; and Marek Voss, the syndicate enforcer assigned to 'assist.' First friction over supplies and authority. Beat: uneasy alliance forming.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. The boat pushes into the Kestrel Basin. Priya reads the river's moods while cataloguing her crewmates' tells, especially Marek's too-practiced competence. They find the first expedition campsite—abandoned in order, not panic. Beat: the mystery sharpening from rumor to evidence.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Tuck, POV. Scanning frequencies at night, Tuck catches a fragment of transmission—Reyes's voice, faint, repeating a bearing upstream. He hides it from Marek and tells only Cyrus. Beat: the thrill and burden of being the one who knows first.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. At a fortified crossing, a warlord called Mother Gant demands payment in information, not goods. She warns them the river above 'eats expeditions' and mentions Meridian by name. Marek pays with a lie so smooth Cyrus can't tell what was traded. Beat: power's casual cruelty on display.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. A flash flood from an unseen tributary nearly capsizes them; they lose half their fuel. Priya realizes the upper basin's weather is behaving impossibly—storms forming against the prevailing winds. Beat: awe curdling into scientific alarm.

chapters.title: The Enforcer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marek, POV. Alone on watch, Marek reviews his secret orders: confirm the deposit exists, then ensure no witnesses return. He hesitates for the first time in years, watching Tuck sleep. Beat: the first crack in a man built for orders.

chapters.title: Meridian's Ghost Camp
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. They find the Meridian base camp intact but stripped of its core instruments, with Reyes's journal describing readings 'no atmosphere should produce.' A fresh set of boot prints leads onward—someone else is following the same trail. Beat: they are not alone, and everyone knows it now.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Tuck, POV. Their own transmitter fails—sabotaged. Tuck traces the damage to someone aboard and says nothing, testing each crewmate quietly. Suspicion poisons meals and watches. Beat: paranoia replacing camaraderie.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Standing Storms
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. The river narrows into a gorge where a permanent storm cell rotates overhead, fed by something below. Priya's instruments confirm it: the source region generates its own weather. Crossing beneath it costs them their spare engine. Beat: confronting nature rewritten by human discovery.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. They find Ilsa Reyes alive—or half-alive—holed up in a cliff cave, the sole survivor, guarding a case of survey cores. She trusts no one, least of all Marek, whom she recognizes as syndicate. At gunpoint, truths come out: the syndicate wants monopoly over predictable weather. Beat: betrayal made explicit; alliances redrawn.

chapters.title: The Case for Burning It
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV (interlude). Reyes explains what the mineral does: localized atmospheric manipulation, stable enough to steer monsoons. Whoever holds the source holds agriculture for three nations. She argues for destruction; Marek argues the knowledge can't be unlearned, only owned. Beat: the moral fault line drawn in open air.

chapters.title: Mother Gant's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Gant's runners catch up—the toll bridge debt was a tracker deal. Gant offers Cyrus passage out and debt forgiveness if he hands over Reyes and the cores. Cyrus stalls, buying a night, and lies to his crew about the terms. Beat: the price of survival made personal and shameful.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Tuck, POV. Tuck discovers Cyrus's lie and exposes it at the worst moment, as Gant's boats close in. The crew splinters: Marek sides with the syndicate openly, Priya with Reyes, Tuck caught between anger at Cyrus and need for him. Beat: trust shattered just before the storm.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The monsoon makes landfall early and violent, trapping both crews in the gorge. In the chaos, Marek saves Tuck from drowning—an act that undoes him—and Gant's forces seize the cores. Beat: catastrophe stripping everyone to their true selves.

chapters.title: What Marek Owes
chapters.summary: Marek, POV. Wounded and marooned with the crew he was ordered to erase, Marek defects fully, revealing the syndicate's extraction plan and Gant's role as their upstream proxy. His confession costs him any claim to forgiveness. Beat: a corrupted man choosing, too late, to be decent.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. They reach the source: a canyon venting charged mineral vapor, the engine of the standing storm. Reyes's data confirms destruction is possible—collapse the vent shaft—but it will trigger the mother of all storms. Someone must stay to arm it manually. Beat: terrible clarity about the cost.

chapters.title: Gant's Last Toll
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Final confrontation at the vent: Gant's fighters versus the crew, with the monsoon raging overhead. Reyes dies arming the charge, passing her journal to Priya. Gant, refusing retreat, is swallowed by the collapsing shaft. Beat: sacrifice answering the question of what survival is worth.

chapters.title: Running Before the Sky
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The induced superstorm erases the source and everything around it. The survivors run the flooded gorge in a crippled boat, Marek navigating waters he has no right to know, Tuck coaxing life from dead radios. Beat: pure momentum, grief and adrenaline fused.

chapters.title: Downriver Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. They drift into Lowmark with no data, no proof, no payday—only Reyes's journal, which Priya will publish as science, not commodity. The syndicate disavows them; the debt is void because there's nothing left to collect against. Beat: poverty accepted as the price of a clean conscience.

chapters.title: Measuring in People
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Weeks later, Cyrus repairs boats in Lowmark, Tuck apprenticed beside him, Marek hauling timber under a new name, Priya writing. When a young chaser asks Cyrus if he misses the storms, he answers honestly: he stopped counting miles the day he started counting the people in the boat. Beat: belonging earned, quiet and final.
